## Summary

I implemented serialized-envelope support in `libs/core/langchain_core/messages/utils.py` with two changes:

1. **`_convert_to_message`** — In the `dict` branch, added a guard that detects the full Serializable constructor-envelope signature (`lc == 1`, `type == "constructor"`, `id` is a `list`, `kwargs` is a `dict`) and delegates to a new helper. Dicts that only partially match fall through to the existing `role`/`type`/`content` handling and error path.

2. **`_create_message_from_envelope`** (new helper) — Extracts the class name from `id[-1]`, strips a trailing `Chunk` so chunk variants map to their parent type, and maps the name to the message class (`HumanMessage`, `AIMessage`, `SystemMessage`, `ChatMessage`, `FunctionMessage`, `ToolMessage`, `RemoveMessage`). It constructs the message directly from `kwargs` (so `content`, `id`, and `tool_calls` are preserved exactly), and for `ToolMessage` lifts an `artifact` out of `additional_kwargs` into the `artifact` attribute. Unknown class names raise `ValueError` with the `MESSAGE_COERCION_FAILURE` error code.

I did not touch anything under `tests/`.
